doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Joining the Messengers and moving to New York
title: Philadelphia with Lee Morgan and quitting Blakey
summary: Ware fears Philly police over scars, meets Lee Morgan, misses a night with a toothache, and returns to New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Our next engagement was, let's see ... Atlantic City; our next engagement I think was Trenton. Yeah, it was Trenton, New Jersey, and then we had another engagement in Philadelphia. Now, I didn't want to go to Philly, because I had heard that the police were so tough on the addicts or people they thought were addicts, and if you had scars on your arm, you'd go to the penitentiary.
Those were the days of Ferguson.

Yeah. Well, anyway, Kenny Drew and I both said, 'Well, man, you got to get somebody else to make that gig.' And he fumed and screamed and said, 'No, you're gonna make it -- I brought you out of Chicago.' So we finally said, 'Okay'. So we come down to Philly and this was when I was introduced to Lee Morgan. Lee made the gig. Back then, he and Lee were very good buddies, and he played at the old Blue Note.
Now we went up ... the thing was on a Wednesday. Now, I had a hole in my tooth that I was walking around with

this little medication with cotton; that you'd stick down and kill that nerve ... for years. I was deathly afraid of dentists. And Friday night, I'll never forget, I started dancing, this tooth went up on me and started aching, and I couldn't play; I was a nervous wreck, and so Spanky played a night, and some night, Art would pay me off and he would say 'Well man, you didn't want to come down here with me' and blah, blah, blah, and I'm gonna change it.

And he said 'What do you want to do? Go back to Chicago?' And I said, 'No, I'm going back to New York'. So I got used to New York, and that was where I went. I went back to New York and I moved out there with somebody out there in Brooklyn, and that was my initiation. Ira I stayed out for awhile in New York and he was married and had three children, and my kids were kind of grown, so we didn't have no hassle that way, and then I was still chasing that powder (inaudible) and trying to work.
